c0-frame.title: Frame the cycle
c0-frame.imperative: Cycle 4: trial (human: 'lets do it!'). The real-issue dogfood: full f1Brainz map extracted and rendered per the ruled pipeline; one unblocked f1Brainz issue worked by a dev agent whose handoff carries the Map entry point per the new skill edits; regen-after-change runs as part of the same trial (the maintenance-loop test). Consumption value and loop viability are the two live unknowns this cycle probes.
c0-frame.finding: flavor=trial (human: 'lets do it!'). Cycle 4 = real-issue dogfood: full map + one unblocked issue + dev agent with map handoff + regen-after-change. Probes the two live unknowns: consumption value, maintenance-loop viability.

prep-fullmap.title: Prep: extract and render the full f1Brainz map
prep-fullmap.imperative: Run the ruled extractor (x7b AST pipeline) over all of f1Brainz src/ plus scripts/ and tests/ (closing the x11 extraction-window gap), run the supplement pass, render agent-lean per-entity pages with render_fn, and emit ids.jsonl. f1Brainz stays READ-ONLY for this step; artifacts land in evidence/x13/map/. Record entity/page/hole counts and wall time as finding.
prep-fullmap.finding: Full map BUILT: 1,224 files (1 BOM parse failure), 515,678 statements, 14,998 entities, 16,222 pages, 38s cold rebuild, deterministic (double-build diff clean), ASCII-clean templates, ids.jsonl established empty. Entry-point page verified: split_half_boundary_drift referenced-by = 3 sites / 3 modules, matches independent AST scan. DEFECT FIXED (D4): function-scoped imports dropped edges to local — 2,046 calls/reads lost across 315 files, including the trial's own entry-point call from pipeline.py; fixed in x13 copy. DEFECTS NAMED NOT FIXED: D2 contains-symbol truncates nesting chain (251 entities, 87 colliding definition sites — store cannot distinguish them; renderer joins on file+line, 14,998/14,998 resolved); D3 wrapped docstring summary renders split (cosmetic, inherited from x11). Resolution 9.26pct unresolved vs 7.55 on the slice (gentle at 180x; 95pct of it dispatch-unknown-base). SCALE FINDINGS: tests hold 61pct of entities and 85pct of test pages carry 'referenced by: none' (true but useless — a noise class needing a rendering policy); src orphan rate 13pct is now REAL signal (window closed); top INDEX at 1,233 lines is NOT a routing surface — needs a second grouping level; entity pages hold their size at scale (median 15 lines, p90 25).

prep-issue.title: Prep: pick one unblocked f1Brainz issue
prep-issue.imperative: Find f1Brainz's issue tracker; list unblocked issues; pick one bounded enough for a single dev-agent dispatch (human: 'pretty much any unblocked issue will do'). Record the pick and why as finding.
prep-issue.finding: PICK: f1Brainz #708 — split_half_boundary_drift (scripts/validate_segment_map_662.py:160) relies on a default telemetry-store path that fails confusingly in worktrees; fix = explicit store arg. WHY: unblocked, bounded (one function + callers), labeled low; and the task IS a blast-radius exercise — callers in src/physics/pilot/pipeline.py and tests/unit/physics/segment_map/derivation/test_segment_map_gating.py span src+scripts+tests, exactly the extraction window x11 flagged as missing and this cycle's full manifest closes. The map's referenced-by line for the function is the direct test of non-grep-recoverable value.

x13.title: Excursion: the dogfood trial — a dev agent works a real issue with the map
x13.imperative: Dispatch a dev agent on the picked issue, on a branch in f1Brainz (never its main). Handoff carries the Map entry point (specific pages for the issue's entities) per the new template pattern, plus the light implementer map-use guidance and the comment grammar (write tagged comments where the change embodies an assumption/constraint/rationale; mint [id] anchors only at need). Capture: whether/how the map was used (trace), whether pages carried non-recoverable facts or got skipped for grep, quality of the change, comments written. Record scoped verdict as finding; the human reads the diff.

x14-regen.title: The maintenance-loop test — regen over the real change
x14-regen.imperative: After x13's change exists: re-run extraction + render over the changed f1Brainz branch, diff the derived store against the pre-change map, and assess: is the diff legible and bounded by the source churn (the minimal design's core claim)? Do any tagged comments written in x13 extract into statements? Does the empty-diff determinism assertion hold on a no-change rebuild? First-ever regen #2 — record everything that surprises as finding.
